passkeys.settings.never.remove.label: Remove {host} from the list

passkeys.settings.off_access_given: Access to https pages is already given, so turning this on does not ask again.
passkeys.settings.recent: Count a recent unlock as verification
passkeys.settings.recent.desc: An unlock in the last 5 minutes counts as checking it is you.
passkeys.settings.recent.hint: With this on, one click is enough to use a passkey right after you unlocked Ferret. Turn it off to be asked to verify every time.
passkeys.settings.reload: Pages that are open now start using Ferret after you load them again.
passkeys.settings.shared: The access to https pages is shared with saving passwords. Turning one off keeps the access while the other is on.
passkeys.settings.signed_out: Ferret is signed out, so passkeys on websites stay with the browser until you sign in.
passkeys.settings.switch.desc: Ferret can save and use passkeys on websites.
passkeys.settings.title: Use Ferret for passkeys
passkeys.settings.why: To offer passkeys, Ferret has to run a small script on every https page, so it asks the browser for access to https pages. The script sends nothing until a website asks for a passkey. Ferret answers only after you choose it in its own window, and the browser is always one of the choices.

passkeys.verify.recent: Ferret was just unlocked: one click is enough.
